extracted.intended_audience: creative writing students and instructors; aspiring fiction writers
extracted.subtask_description: Core craft-and-evaluation checklist drawn from Janet Burroway's Writing Fiction, summarizing chapter-topics and major quality criteria for producing and judging short/long fiction. Emphasizes scene, character, image, point-of-view, plot, and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whatever Works (the writing process)
rubrics_metrics.description: The writing process: pragmatic, flexible approaches to generating and shaping material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on finding an individualized process — experimentation and methods that enable production and revision. Treats craft as practice rather than one-size-fits-all rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing Not Telling (concrete sensory detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor concrete, sensory detail and dramatized scene over summary or exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use image, action, dialogue, and specific sensory detail to convey experience; reserve telling/summary for moments when compression or commentary is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building Character — direct vs. indirect characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for creating character: direct statement versus indirect revelation through behavior, speech, and detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer indirect characterization (showing through desire, action, contradiction) but know when direct description can be useful; balance helps realism and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Flesh Made Word (character continued — desire, contradiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Character development centered on desire and contradiction: wants that drive action and internal inconsistencies that create complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should be propelled by clear wants; contradictions make characters interesting and believable. Desire provides motivation for plot and scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long Ago and Far Away (setting, atmosphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use setting and atmosphere to ground story, influence mood, and shape character action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific, sensory settings create resonance; setting can act on characters and be integral to plot, not mere backdrop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Form, Plot, and Structure (Aristotle, Freytag, contemporary forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand classical and contemporary narrative structures (Aristotelian unity, Freytag's arc, modern forms) and how plot is organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot conceived as pattern of conflict leading to crisis and resolution; structure choices should support character arcs and thematic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call Me Ishmael (point of view)
rubrics_metrics.description: Point of view (POV): choices about narrator, focalization, and voice; maintain consistency and make intentional shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POV must be controlled—avoid accidental head-hopping; legal, ethical, or ironic distance of narrator should be a deliberate craft choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is and Is Not (theme, image, symbol, metaphor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of theme and figurative language: theme as resonance rather than didactic message; use of image, symbol, and metaphor to carry meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theme should emerge organically through image and action; avoid preaching—show thematic resonance through recurring images and implicative detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play It Again, Sam (revision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision as essential craft: re-seeing, restructuring, and refining language, scene, and character after initial drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision includes pruning, reordering, tightening language, and re-evaluating POV/plot; it's where specificity and dramatic choices are honed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant detail — concrete, definite, specific, sensory
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer details that are concrete, definite, specific, and sensory to create vividness and meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant details both engage the senses and carry narrative or thematic weight; avoid vague abstractions that flatten scene and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing: scene, image, dialogue, action
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary showing techniques include fully realized scenes, strong images, revealing dialogue, and active behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scene to dramatize conflict; images should bear meaning; dialogue must do character work and move plot; action should reveal character and escalate stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telling: when summary is right
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary (telling) has a rightful place when compression, transitions, or commentary are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know when to summarize to skip unimportant material or to provide necessary background without slowing narrative; balancing showing and telling is a craft choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active not passive verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor active verbs and strong syntax to create immediacy and energy in prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive passive constructions that distance the reader; choose verbs that carry agency and consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character via desire — what the character wants drives the story
rubrics_metrics.description: A character's wants (desires, needs, goals) should drive choices, conflict, and forward motion of the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make desires concrete and compelling; plot grows out of characters pursuing and being obstructed in pursuit of those wants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character via contradiction — interesting characters are inconsistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should contain contradictions and complexity rather than consistent, one-note traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contradictions to create inner conflict, unpredictability, and depth; avoid flatness by allowing characters to act against type when believable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot = pattern of conflict, crisis, resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot is conceptualized as a sequence or pattern of conflicts that escalate to crises and are followed by resolution (or lack thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure scenes and story units to increase pressure and consequence; crises should feel inevitable yet surprising given character choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: POV consistency and intentional shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain point-of-view consistency, and when shifts occur they must be intentional and clearly signaled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accidental POV slips break immersion; planned shifts can be used for irony, contrast, or expanding scope but require craft to manage smoothly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme as resonance, not message
rubrics_metrics.description: Theme should function as resonance—patterns of meaning arising from image, action, and character — not as didactic statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow theme to emerge from the work's elements; avoid stating a moral or lesson overtly. Let implications and echoes accumulate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image as the load-bearing unit of meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Images (concrete sensory units) carry the weight of meaning in fiction; they hold thematic, emotional, and narrative load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop recurring or striking images that connect to character and theme; use image to condense complex resonances into evocative detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image (element of imaginative writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of Burroway's five shared elements: image — sensory, particular detail that creates experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images should be concrete and carry associative weight across the piece; they are essential across fiction, poetry, drama, and CNF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (element of imaginative writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five elements: voice — the narrative personality or diction that shapes how material is presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice encompasses tone, register, and the narrator's perspective; it must be consistent and appropriate to story and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character (element of imaginative writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five elements: character — the persons (or focal minds) whose wants, contradictions, and choices make story possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character work includes desires, contradictions, and growth; characters should be active agents whose inner life is revealed through action and detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting (element of imaginative writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five elements: setting — the physical, social, and historical context that shapes action and mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting ought to be specific and integrated into plot and character; use atmosphere to influence tone and stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story (element of imaginative writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five elements: story — the sequence of events and their causal/psychological logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story combines plot, character motivation, and structure; maintain causal clarity while allowing for complexity and resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity is the soul of narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Mantra: specificity—precise, particular detail—fundamentally animates narrative and reader engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise nouns, concrete gestures, and distinct images to create verisimilitude and emotional truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: A story is a war
rubrics_metrics.description: Mantra/metaphor: stories are contests of desire and opposition, framed as conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach story as struggle—characters face antagonism (internal, interpersonal, or external) that must be addressed; conflict drives stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Trouble' is the fundamental story unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Mantra: 'trouble'—moments of difficulty or complication—are the basic building blocks of narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek to create and escalate trouble in scenes to sustain forward momentum; trouble reveals character and produces plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant detail engages the senses, conveys atmosphere, conveys story
rubrics_metrics.description: Mantra reiteration: well-chosen details should simultaneously engage senses, set atmosphere, and advance story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select details that do double (or triple) duty — sensory immediacy plus narrative or thematic function — rather than decorative or neutral description.
